quaternius-outfits-v1.reason: Flat-colour modular garments. Split across the jrpg-bases.md 60/30/10 blocking: the peasant set is the 60 (fur), the ranger set the 30 (accent), and the bare 'Regular' body material is the 15-25% skin.

quaternius-monsters-v1.reason: Flat-colour slots, one primitive per material, so every region recolours independently. *_Main is the base coat, *_Secondary the accent — except on the three chibi kemono bipeds (cat/bunny/frog) where the secondary IS the lighter belly/muzzle countershade kemono.md describes, so it maps to innerMuzzle.

quaternius-animals-v1.reason: Head/tail DONOR pack (quadruped rigs). Mapped for completeness and for the fox/wolf head-graft follow-up; no lane registers these as a basis today (see blocked[] below).

unverifiedSlots.Material: The Husky ships five unnamed Blender-default materials. Assigned by slot order (base coat, light, accent, detail, dark) WITHOUT a visual check — flagged rather than presented as verified.

vroid-cc0-v1.reason: VRoid names every material with a role suffix (_SKIN/_FACE/_EYE/_HAIR/_CLOTH), so the mapping is exact rather than heuristic. Used when the house toon shader replaces MToon on the web path (technique.md: MToon on WebGL2 is unverified upstream).

godette-v1.reason: Four named materials on a 3.4k-tri anime mascot — the cheapest anime avatar we ship and the one that fits the Quest-3 budget with room to spare.

kaykit-adventurers-v1.reason: SINGLE 1024-class baked atlas per character and NO named material slots, so swap_materials() cannot reach it: binding that one material to a flat house colour paints the whole character one colour. That is why this pack shipped with recolour switched off, recorded as a capability gap whose fix 'needs the atlas cell layout, an art task'. It is not an art task. The atlas is PALETTE-INDEXED (measured: PNG colortype 3, 198-256 entries) and the vendor splits every character into SEMANTIC MESH NODES, so each node's texels are a luminance ramp of one hue - the Knight's head is a 16-entry flesh ramp, its cape a 13-entry red one. The region colour therefore replaces the HUE per node while the atlas keeps supplying the SHADING, with no new texture and no re-UVing. The engine measures each node's dominant hue and how much of the node it covers, and recolours only texels near that hue - a node that mixes two materials (the Mage's 'Head' node is 36% single-hue because it carries the hood AND the face) keeps its vendor colours rather than being painted one wrong colour. mount_report().atlasRegions says exactly what recoloured.

kaykit-skeletons-v1.reason: Same single-atlas texturing and the same semantic mesh-node split as the Adventurers pack, so the same per-node recolour applies. The skeletons additionally separate Skull/Jaw/Eyes as their own nodes, which is why the bone tone and the socket glow recolour independently.

polygonalmind-100avatars-v1.reason: NO per-part boundary exists on these avatars, and that was measured across all 8 rather than assumed: one mesh node, one primitive, one material, no COLOR_0, no VRM firstPerson/blendShape/spring-bone annotation, and UV islands that are ANATOMICAL (94 large islands carrying only 23 distinct dominant colours between them). So there is nothing to bind a region to. What IS a material partition is the texture: each avatar resolves to just 2-4 BASE COLOURS. The engine measures those at mount time and classifies every texel to the nearest, taking its region from regionOrder by AREA - the jrpg-bases.md 60/30/10 blocking, so the biggest colour is the base coat. Measured accuracy ~88% of texels; the margin gate leaves ambiguous texels on the vendor colour rather than guessing, and misassignment is mostly benign because a dark texel lands on a dark region. Works on the two JPEG-textured avatars too: being non-indexed blocks an index->region LUT, not classification.

khronos-fox-v1.reason: One textured material on a 576-tri quadruped; it is the runtime-loader reference asset, not a player avatar.

blocked.wanted: The CC0 'Base Rigged Stylized Humanoid Character (YW)' as a second anime base.
blocked.verdict: NOT VENDORED - the archive contains no format anything here can read.
blocked.evidence: The only geometry in the OGA archive is a .blend file — no FBX/glTF/DAE export exists.
blocked.blocker: Blender, or any other reader of the .blend format, and none is reachable here. .blend is a proprietary binary dump of Blender's in-memory structures; Godot cannot import it, GLTFDocument cannot parse it, and nothing in tools/asset-pipeline reads it. The usual escape hatch is the `bpy` PyPI wheel, which was checked rather than assumed: this machine has no pip at all and runs Python 3.14, for which no bpy wheel is published. Unlike the animal-head graft - where the data needed was already sitting in the GLB's bone weights - there is no alternative data path, because the geometry exists ONLY inside that one file.
blocked.shippedInstead: The two VRoid CC0 bases plus Godette cover the anime lane.

unlaned.quaternius-animals-v1: Vendored as HEAD/TAIL DONOR geometry for the kemono graft, which the blocked[] entry below proves is not possible at runtime: every quadruped is one skinned mesh with no separable head node. They are quadrupeds, not avatars, so they are deliberately not offered as playable characters either. Kept because they remain the donor set the moment a Blender-equipped pipeline exists.
unlaned.khronos-fox-v1: The canonical quadruped skinning/animation reference asset for the runtime GLB loader tests (576 tris, mixed CC0 mesh / CC-BY-4.0 rig). A test fixture, never a player avatar.
